steps.what: Evaluate client evidence and differential explanations in the family context
Diagnose mental and emotional disorders and discuss conclusions within professional authority

tasks.design: Retain therapist evaluation, diagnosis and explanation to the client. Existing assessment evidence in {DOCS} supports the judgement; documentation assistance does not establish diagnostic accuracy or shorten clinical deliberation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Diagnosis depends on context, differential explanations and the reliability of evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: No validated diagnostic replacement is supplied in the digest.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting accounts, changing symptoms and family-system effects.
tasks.human_edge: Integrate evidence without reducing the person to a symptom label.
tasks.altitude: Diagnostic responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Discuss clinical formulation across care roles

evidence.claim: Clinical diagnosis remains contextual professional judgement; the digest's note-drafting tools do not establish diagnostic automation or a local saving.

assumptions: Boundary is evidence synthesis and diagnostic conclusion, excluding separate information collection, treatment and note production. Client interviewing is owned by the collection task and not counted again here.

Therapist produces formulation and conclusion in s1 and s2 with full time retained. Client information collection supplies underlying evidence; no structured diagnosis flag or model-generated clinical truth is assumed.
Use native evidence access first. Unchanged judgement adds no incremental upkeep. Professional scope and national diagnostic rules require local confirmation.
research_questions: Which uncertainties require additional assessment before a diagnostic conclusion is appropriate?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=60+40=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Formulation, diagnosis and explanation retain time; note-drafting savings are not assigned to clinical decisions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Confer with clients to develop feasible posttreatment activity plans

tasks.design: Keep posttreatment planning as collaborative discussion with the client. Existing care information in {DOCS} can support the conversation, while goals, readiness and workable support arrangements remain jointly considered human decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans depend on the client's actual priorities, resources and relationships.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability removes collaborative planning work.
tasks.still_hard: Uncertain support, conflicting goals and changing circumstances after treatment.
tasks.human_edge: Develop a plan the client understands and can realistically use.
tasks.altitude: Planning dialogue and clinical responsibility remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Posttreatment planning remains collaborative clinical work; note generation does not establish a reduction in this conversation.

assumptions: Boundary is client planning dialogue, excluding separately maintained progress notes and external support delivery. No standalone paperwork baseline is invented.
Therapist and client produce the plan through the retained discussion. No pre-existing structured readiness or support-availability flag is assumed.
Use native care-information access first. No changed workflow adds upkeep.
research_questions: Which support arrangements need clarification before the client can rely on the plan?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Collaborative planning retains full time; progress-note automation is outside this task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect client information through assessment and discussion

steps.what: Collect client information using appropriate testing, interviewing, discussion or observation

tasks.design: Retain client interviewing, observation, discussion and appropriately selected testing. Existing assessment material in {DOCS} supports the encounter; recording or note drafting does not replace the work of eliciting and understanding information.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reliable evidence depends on rapport, observation and suitable assessment methods.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest supports documentation assistance, without evidence that these encounters can be shortened.
tasks.still_hard: Contradictory accounts, sensitive disclosures and incomplete understanding.
tasks.human_edge: Notice what requires clarification and adapt questions to the person and family context.

evidence.claim: Interviewing, testing and observation remain human collection work; clinical note products do not establish an encounter-time reduction.

assumptions: Boundary is information elicitation and observation, excluding later diagnostic formulation, treatment and separate note production. Testing, interviewing and observation are alternative or combined methods, not three mandatory sequential encounters.

Therapist produces assessment evidence through the fully retained step; client supplies accounts during existing contact. No complete structured symptom input, automatic test validity or emotion inference is assumed.
Use native assessment materials first. No introduced system creates upkeep; professional and national testing requirements remain local facts.
research_questions: Which apparent information gaps require another conversation rather than automated completion?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Information elicitation and observation retain all time; no transcription baseline is assigned to the encounter.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather evidence for custody or visitation recommendations

steps.what: Establish the court question, information scope and authorised professional contacts
Gather information from doctors, schools, social workers and other relevant professionals
Evaluate gathered evidence for recommendations on custody or visitation disputes

tasks.design: Retain scoped professional evidence gathering and the therapist's recommendation analysis. Source-attributed material in {DOCS} supports evaluation; no model decides which account is true or recommends a custody outcome.
tasks.previous_blocker: Court-related recommendations require careful scope, source attribution and evaluation of conflicting evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest's social-care note tools do not establish validated custody assessment capability.
tasks.still_hard: Different professional accounts, disputed facts and limits of the therapist's mandate.
tasks.human_edge: Explain the strength and limitations of evidence without overstating certainty.
tasks.altitude: Evidence gathering and recommendation responsibilities remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Mandate, disclosure scope and evidence limitations

evidence.claim: Source attribution and contextual evaluation remain human work in court-related evidence gathering; model knowledge does not justify transferring social-care note savings to custody recommendations.

assumptions: Boundary is therapist scoping, gathering and recommendation analysis within an established mandate, excluding other professionals' source production, court decisions and separate formal report preparation or issue.

Therapist produces the request scope in s1 and attributed evidence in s2, retaining full capture and clarification time. Each professional is the existing producer of their account or record; no new structured submission is imposed. Missing or disputed evidence remains explicit rather than filled automatically.
Use native secure document access first. No changed process adds upkeep. Applicable national court, confidentiality and professional rules and the mandate must be confirmed locally.
research_questions: Which material contradictions must be resolved or explicitly qualified before a recommendation can be made?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+45+25=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Scope, evidence collection and recommendation judgement retain time; outside professionals and court work are excluded.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: These clinical and court-related tasks retain their human effort; documentation capabilities do not establish savings in assessment or professional judgement.
reach: Coordinate attributed evidence with child and family social workers
Discuss assessment limits with mental health counselors
role.ambitious_version: A therapist who makes clinical and court-related conclusions traceable to assessed evidence while preserving client relationships and clear professional limits.
